task: Round 10, narrow target: .agent-harness/scripts/check_canary_freshness.py at HEAD 32ba566, its wiring into validate_harness.py, and the C7 attestation it certifies. Nothing else. Background: four canaries (C1/C4/C5/C6) died because an attestation outlived the code it attested and nothing checked it. Commit 32ba566 added this detector, which found C5 and C6 stale on its first run, and dispatched a fresh C7 that supersedes both. Your job is to make a stale canary pass, or to make a fresh one fail, and to prove either executably against real unmodified scripts. Attack ideas to exhaust rather than a checklist: the supersedes_canary field is self-asserted by the very artifact whose freshness is in question, so can a stale canary supersede ITSELF, or can two stale canaries supersede each other in a cycle so that neither is ever live, or can a fabricated attestation retire a real one? canary_id() falls back to inferring the id from the run directory name -- can that inference be driven to collide two canaries, or to produce an id that no supersedes_canary can ever name? NON_FILE_DIGESTS excludes result_sha256, assignment_sha256 and token_digest from being treated as attested files, so can a real hook digest be smuggled under one of those names and thereby escape checking? ATTESTED_FILES is a closed map, so what happens to a canary that attests a hook not in it, and is the failure direction right? find_attestations only globs runs/*/artifacts/*.json -- can an attestation be placed where the glob does not reach while still reading to a human as retained evidence? is the check reachable at all when validate_harness runs in a tree with no runs directory, and is that the safe direction? Verify C7 itself against the retained bytes: does the bracket actually contain the consume instant, is the claimed 44.8 ms real, was ACTIVE_RUN really pointing at the decoy, and is the retained BLOCKED first attempt consistent with the story told about it. Report the attacks that FAILED too, with exact inputs.
